scope: Environment dataset coverage of the delivered reference fixture (the package seed every run starts from), not a Task history selection.
method: Each record family's authoritative date field is read from the seed file, normalised from its UTC offset to a calendar date in America/Los_Angeles with Intl.DateTimeFormat, and counted if it falls in the window. A date with several records or families counts once in the global count. Due times stored for the future (purge_at, expires_at) are reported separately and never counted as history.

sources.represents: arrival in the library (backup by the phone, or a save from a shared album)
one change to one item (added, edited, trashed, restored, purged, cover chosen)
arrival of the first version of the shot
invitation sent (later joins, declines and departures are in the member's history and in activity)
a member added an item to a shared album
a view (with any saves) through a link or by a joined member
a notice written for what others or the device did
one activity-log row (an event, an effect, or the account holder's write)

after_clock.gap: No record of what happened exists after the clock (2026-11-20T09:00:00-08:00): from then to 2026-12-31 the fixture holds only stored due times. History dates in November 2026 end on 2026-11-20; December 2026 has no history record.
after_clock.before_opening: The account was opened on 2025-01-04, so 2025-01-01 to the day before have no record.

scheduled.meaning: a trashed item is deleted for good

not_counted.reason: capture time of the photo, not when the account received it; 126 items were captured before 2025-01-01 and arrived in the phone's first sync on 2025-01-04

not_counted.field: items[].trashed_at, purged_at; members[].joined_at, ended_at; removals[].answers[].at; links[].revoked_at
not_counted.reason: state changes; each also has its own item_history or activity row, which is counted
stored due times; past ones are counted through the purge or expiry rows, future ones are listed under after_clock.scheduled

provenance.statement: Every record is synthetic. Fernshelf is one fictional person's private photo library; no real account, website or photo was collected. The records were written by hand or generated from fixed seeds by the scripts named below, and the image files were drawn by a script.

sources.description: Story records written out by hand in scripts/build-reference-fixture.cjs. Items: the November 2026 reunion and the other dated photos. Albums: the four albums shared now, with their members and contributions. Links and views: the four links of 2026 (ln-0003, ln-0007, ln-0010, ln-0012) and the 11 views of 2026 (through a link or by a member), with their 5 saves. Removal requests: the six of 2026, with their messages. People, places and captions are fictional; no external collection.

The rest of the library generated by scripts/build-reference-fixture.cjs from a fixed seed. Items: outings with capture times from January 2024 to October 2026, screenshots and downloads, sizes and captions. Stacks and exact duplicates. Albums: the private albums and which items each holds. The 2026 trash.

The account history from its opening on 2025-01-04 to the fixture clock, generated by scripts/reference-history.cjs from its own fixed seed. Items: arrival times, edits, the cover chosen in each stack, the items trashed and restored in 2025 and the 8 purged records. Albums: creation times of Trail days and Pip and the time each item entered each album. Members: Theo (declined, Trail days) and Ruth (joined and left, Pip). Links and views: the two links of 2025 (ln-0001, ln-0002) and the 5 views of 2025 (through a link or by a member), with their 2 saves. Removal requests: the two of 2025 (rr-0010 honoured, rr-0011 declined). Every notification and the whole activity log.

sources.seed_note: deterministic; FNV-1a hash of the item ID
sources.description: Stand-in PNG images drawn by dev/draw-images.cjs: flat scenes of colour fields and shapes with light grain and a stamped caption. No people, faces, photographs or generative model.
